notes: The Memsic 2125 straddles the breadboard centre gap in columns 17-19. Top row: GND.1 (17), YOUT (18), TOUT (19); bottom row: GND.2 (17), XOUT (18), VDD (19). This mapping is inferred from the circuit image and schematic.

The breadboard image labels the top half rows f-j and the bottom half rows a-e. The catalogue names the top half bank 't' (rows a-e) and the bottom half bank 'b' (rows f-j), so I used the catalogue naming.

Column and rail numbers are estimated from the image. The Arduino GND wire lands at bn.5. The two black wires from the module land at bn.10 and bn.13 on the bottom negative rail, which joins all the grounds.
The Temp (TOUT) pin is not connected to anything, as in the manual.
The Arduino 5V and GND wires go to the power header sockets on the board. I used GND.1 for GND.
The Arduino connects to a computer by USB for serial output. The manual doesn't draw this, so it is not in the graph.
